cards.text: David, who would later become king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), wrote this song, and its heading tells you when. Saul, Israel's king (1 Samuel 11:15), had sent men to watch David's house in order to kill him. David is talking to God here, and he's got a lot to say.

cards.question: Saul's men are watching David's house. What's the first thing David asks God for?

answers.text: To deliver him from his enemies
To give him a sword to fight back
To help him make peace with Saul

cards.text: He says it again: save me from men of bloodshed. Then he tells God to look at them lying in wait, and I bet his heart is pounding.

cards.question: Fierce men are plotting against David. David says it's for no sin of his own.

cards.text: No fault of his own, and they're rushing to attack him anyway. Then David prays: "Arise to help me, and take notice."

cards.question: David calls on the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, to rouse Himself to punish all the nations. What does David ask for the wicked traitors?

cards.text: Then David describes what's out there: his enemies return in the evening, snarling like dogs. Me, I'd be under the blanket, and then under the blanket's BLANKET.

cards.question: David's enemies come back in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the ___.

cards.text: And David says, look what spews out of their mouths: sharp words from their lips. SHARP, friend. Sharper than my edges were by the time I got slid into the back of the junk drawer, and okay, that's a LOW bar.

cards.question: David's enemies are spewing sharp words. What do they say that shows what they're thinking?

answers.text: They think nobody can hear them
They think David will give up
They think the king will reward them

cards.question: David says the LORD is afraid of the men prowling around his house.

cards.text: Then David says, "But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations."
Then the song shifts from the enemies to God. David calls Him his strength and his fortress.

cards.question: Saul's men are watching David's house. But David says he will keep watch for ___.

cards.text: Then he says it straight: my God of loving devotion will come to meet me. Not might, not maybe, WILL.

cards.question: David says God will let him stare down his foes.

cards.text: Then David asks God NOT to kill them. Wait, WHAT, men sent to kill him and he says don't kill them?

cards.question: Why does David ask God not to kill his enemies?

answers.text: So his enemies can turn back
So he can show them mercy

cards.text: Instead, he asks God to scatter them by His power and bring them down. And he calls Him "O Lord, our shield."

cards.question: David's enemies have been spewing sharp words. What does David ask for them to be trapped in?

cards.text: Then he asks God to consume them in wrath, till they are no more. And he says what he wants people to know: that God rules over Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28).

cards.question: David wants it known that God rules over Jacob. How far does he want it known?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth

cards.text: That line again: they return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city, scavenging for food and growling if they aren't satisfied. Friend, that's me staring down an oven timer with four minutes left.

cards.question: David's enemies come back in the evening, snarling like dogs. But David says he will proclaim God's loving devotion in the ___.
David calls God his refuge, but only when times are easy.

cards.text: He finishes singing praises with names he's already given God: O my strength, my fortress, my God of loving devotion. Enemies prowling the city and David's SINGING, while I spent years in the back of a junk drawer and didn't so much as hum.
